correctness.rationale: A homogeneous polynomial zero on full E_u vanishes on the entire hyperplane, so linear factor u·x divides it; for two nonparallel hyperplanes the factors are coprime and a cubic is uniquely (u·x)(v·x)(w·x). Its Laplacian equals 2[(cI+vu^T+uv^T)w]·x, whose eigenvalues are c (d−2-fold), 1+2c, 2c−1; therefore singular only c=0 or ±1/2. For coincident equators write p=t(at²+t b·y+yᵀCy); harmonicity gives b=0, tr C=−3a, hence d(d−1)/2 free parameters. Independent exact SymPy determinant/rank reconstructions for d=3,4,5,6 and special/generic angles corroborate but do not replace the algebraic all-d proof.

final_claim: Two full equatorial restrictions determine all complex homogeneous harmonic cubics in R^d, d≥3, for distinct equators except right angle (nullity d−2) and 60° (nullity 1); coincident equators nullity d(d−1)/2.
limitations: Requires complete noiseless equatorial traces, pure degree 3, d≥3; no finite sampling or stability bound.
